newsitem.title: FINLAND: Soft Euro may prompt EMU delay - senior Finnish MP.
newsitem.headline: Soft Euro may prompt EMU delay - senior Finnish MP.

text.p: A senior Finnish parliamentarian said on Thursday his country may be in favour of delaying EMU if key EU countries fail to meet the entry criteria, raising prospects for a weak common currency.

"It is possible that most, even including some central EU member countries will not fulfil the criteria for monetary union," pro-EMU conservative Kimmo Sasi, chairman of the tax section of parliament's state finance committee, said in a statement.
"In these conditions it is possible that a soft euro would be created with a level of interest rates clearly higher than the current German interest rate level," he said.
"The question might come up for consideration whether Finland should for its part consider to contribute to a delay in the transfer to a single currency," Sasi said.
Sasi, also member of the Bank of Finland's board of parliamentary supervisors, is regarded as a politician with solid knowledge of EMU issues.
